skills.name: product-build-loop
skills.description: Builds a clickable web prototype of a new product, or adds a module to a prototype that exists, in one unattended run. It asks every question once, gives a local link before it builds, builds and reviews every module, checks every click in a real browser, makes a link per demo state, and hands over. Use when someone types /product-build-loop, or asks to "build a prototype of", "make a clickable demo of", "start a new product", "add a module to my prototype", "mock up an app for" or "build this end to end". Not for restyling screens that already exist or working through screenshot notes (the design loop does that), and not for deciding what to build (the research loop does that).

skills.name: product-research-loop
skills.description: Decides what to build before anyone builds it. Researches the rival products in a category on their public pages, builds a capability sheet (Excel and CSV) with a source link on every cell, searches each rival's own site before calling anything "no rival has it", thinks the product through for its persona, and ends in a product brief with a ranked module list. Use when someone asks "what should we build first", "which modules does X need", "benchmark us against A, B and C", "research the competitors", "make a feature matrix" or "decide the feature set". Not for building the product (the build loop does that) or for a deck about one company (the deck loop does that).

skills.name: product-design-loop
skills.description: Changes how existing screens of a prototype look and work, from one set of notes, and runs to the end without asking again. Three ways in - a list of notes or screenshot comments ("rows too tight", "rename this", "this button does nothing"), a redesign of named screens, or copying a screen from a reference (a video, a web page, screenshots, a design file). Use when someone types /product-design-loop, sends design notes or screenshots of a prototype to change, asks to "rework", "restyle", "polish these screens" or "make this screen look like" a reference. Not for building a new product or new modules (the build loop), and not for a review of the whole product (the review loop).

skills.name: product-review-loop
skills.description: Reviews a whole clickable prototype screen by screen, as the person who will use it, fixes what it finds, and reviews again until no P1 problem is left. It clicks every button, takes a screenshot of every screen, and checks for dead clicks, console errors, cut-off text, placeholder text, broken images, missing empty states, spacing slips, mixed words and pages that scroll sideways on a phone. Use when someone types /product-review-loop, or asks to "review", "audit", "QA", "polish" or "check everything" in a prototype or demo before showing it, or asks "what is wrong with my prototype". Not for a list of notes on named screens (the design loop) or for building new screens (the build loop).

skills.name: product-deck-loop
skills.description: Makes a deck, one-pager, brochure or simple web page for a meeting with a company, end to end. Researches the company, its industry and the people in the meeting with a source link on every fact, writes a story with one idea per slide, builds it, checks every claim and word, and makes an HTML deck, an editable PowerPoint and a PDF. Use when someone asks for "a deck for my meeting with X", "slides for a first meeting", "an outside-in view on a company", "add 3 slides to this deck for X", "a one-pager for a prospect" or "turn this into an editable PowerPoint". Not for research on a product category (the research loop) or for screens of a product (the build loop).
